flags.note: C3 applies only to performance of a portfolio 'other than a private fund.' The subject is a Delaware LP relying on Section 3(c)(7) with a $1,000,000 minimum for qualified purchasers (Slide 9), i.e., a private fund, so the 1-/5-/10-year prescribed periods are not required; the flag's own text concedes this ('for a private fund'). The quoted line also raises no C2 issue: gross and net appear in adjacent columns with equal prominence for every year and the annualized row, and the fee basis (1.5% management fee, fund expenses, 20% incentive allocation subject to high-water mark) is disclosed.

The cover line is a neutral description of strategy and universe, not a statement of benefits requiring counterbalance. In any event the draft already carries the precise risks the flag says are absent: Slide 10 states the investment is speculative and may result in loss of the entire investment, that short selling exposes the Fund to theoretically unlimited losses, that leverage magnifies losses, that small- and mid-cap securities can be illiquid and volatile, and that withdrawals are restricted; the index paragraph likewise notes the Fund sells short and uses leverage. C9's requirement is satisfied.
